title: Stop rebuilding all seven sites for every Papyrus release that does not affect them
description:
Facts: each site rebuild is 10–14 min; a Papyrus version bump across seven sites ≈ 84 min ≈ $0.84; Papyrus released many times in October (check `gh release list -R AnthusAI/Papyrus --limit 50`).
Steps:
1. Measure (read-only): for each site, count October main builds whose commit is a dependency bump (`git log --grep "papyrus" --since 30.days` on main, or Renovate/Dependabot author) vs content/feature commits. Post the split on this story.
2. Options, pick from the data: (a) batch bumps: one weekly bump PR per site (Renovate `schedule` or the bump script) instead of per release; (b) classify releases: the Papyrus release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, semantic-release) labels a release `affects-sites` only when `packages/papyrus`, build-specs or the Python newsroom runtime changed; bump bots (if any) consume that; (c) for pure backend/infra releases, sites skip the bump entirely. Recommended default: (a) + (b) together, no numeric cap.
3. Implement the chosen option in Papyrus (release.yml, scripts) and in each site's bump mechanism; document in docs/site-hosting.md.
Acceptance: Gherkin "a Papyrus release that changes only the Python CLI does not trigger site rebuilds"; the next week's site build count drops; before/after in a comment.
